title: Tool Contracts & Reliable Actions
description: Study typed tool inputs and outputs, idempotency and side effects, timeouts, retries and circuit breakers, and compensation and human checkpoints. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Typed tool inputs and outputs
lessons.description: Specify validation checks beyond JSON parsing.
lessons.conceptOverview: Tool schemas constrain structure, while runtime validation enforces semantics such as valid account ownership and allowed ranges. Return structured error categories so orchestration can distinguish repairable inputs from denied actions.
lessons.whyItMatters: Schema-valid inputs still require authorization and semantic validation.

lessons.title: Idempotency and side effects
lessons.description: Describe how to retry the uncertain request and later reconcile its status.
lessons.conceptOverview: An idempotency key identifies one logical operation across retries. The service must store or reconcile its outcome; inventing a new key on every retry defeats duplicate protection.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reuse the logical operation's idempotency key for uncertain retries.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: An idempotency key identifies one logical operation across retries. The service must store or reconcile its outcome; inventing a new key on every retry defeats duplicate protection.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: An idempotency key identifies one logical operation across retries. The service must store or reconcile its outcome; inventing a new key on every retry defeats duplicate protection.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A payment request times out after the server commits. Retrying with a fresh key can create a second payment.

lessons.title: Timeouts, retries and circuit breakers
lessons.description: Write different retry policies for these two tools.
lessons.conceptOverview: Set deadlines per operation, retry only appropriate failures with bounded backoff, and use circuit breakers to stop repeated calls to unhealthy dependencies. A timeout does not prove the remote action failed.
lessons.whyItMatters: Retry policy depends on side effects and failure semantics.

lessons.title: Compensation and human checkpoints
lessons.description: Identify which steps can be compensated and where review should occur.
lessons.conceptOverview: Multi-step actions may require compensating operations instead of a true rollback. Some effects cannot be undone, so place review checkpoints before commitment and record partial completion clearly.
lessons.whyItMatters: Workflow recovery must distinguish reversible and irreversible effects.
